entities.summary:
Stanford University, founded in 1885 in Palo Alto, California by railroad magnate Leland Stanford in memory of his son, is the world's most entrepreneurially productive university, having created or incubated companies including Google, Yahoo, Hewlett-Packard, Netflix, LinkedIn, and hundreds of others. The university's proximity to Silicon Valley and its culture of faculty entrepreneurship made it the intellectual engine of the technology revolution.

Leland Stanford and his wife Jane established the university with a $5 million endowment and revolutionary mandate: to produce useful graduates rather than gentlemen scholars. The university opened in 1891 with 555 students and free tuition (maintained until 1920). Founding president David Starr Jordan's pragmatic educational philosophy aligned perfectly with California's entrepreneurial culture, establishing a partnership with technology that would define the 20th century.

Stanford's Industrial Park (1951), created by Frederick Terman, housed Hewlett-Packard and became the template for university-industry partnerships creating Silicon Valley. Google was invented in Stanford's computer science building; Yahoo by Stanford students; the concept of the integrated circuit developed by Stanford-connected researchers. The Hoover Institution at Stanford became a major conservative policy research center. With an endowment exceeding $37 billion, Stanford's per-student research spending exceeds any other university.
